name: South Korea (Republic of Korea)

areaKm2.note: world_1945 "Korea (USA)" polygon ~90,800 km2 on the sphere (low); the zone south of the 38th parallel was ~93,600 km2 (standard figure, mid).

population.note: COW NMC v7 tpop ROK 1950 = 20,357k; OWID (HYDE/UN) South Korea 1950 = 19.76M (low); 1949 census ~20.2M.

urbanization.note: OWID (HYDE) urban share South Korea 1950 = 21.4%; COW upop/tpop = 3,127/20,357 = 0.15 (cities over 100,000 only, low).

activePersonnel.note: ROK MND Institute for Military History (6.25 War History vol. 1, 2004): ROK armed forces 105,752 on 25 June 1950, about half the KPA (also the Operation Pokpung infobox). Army ~97,000 (8 divisions, 4 on the parallel), navy 6,956 (ROK Navy article, NHC), air force 1,800 (ROKAF article). Korean War article: 95,000 troops on 25 June, under 22,000 left five days later. National Police (~48,000) excluded.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess: Youth corps, police and recently discharged men usable as fillers; the ROK had no organised reserve divisions and rebuilt from stragglers, police and hasty conscripts in July 1950.

supportPersonnel.note: Remainder after the infantry: navy 6,956, air force 1,800, divisional artillery (91 howitzers), engineers, signals, service troops, the Seoul HQ and schools. Vehicle holdings were only 52% of TO&E (MND).

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess: ROK forces grew to ~590,000 by 1953 after very heavy 1950-51 losses from ~20M people: 0.04-0.06 including replacements.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Rifle troops of 8 infantry divisions (several with only two regiments) plus the Capital Division and independent regiments: ~97,000 army x ~0.55-0.65 infantry share. Reconstruction from the MND total; a third of the frontline troops were on weekend pass on 25 June (MND).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: US WWII small arms; 57 mm AT guns and 2.36 in. bazookas could not stop the T-34; 15% of weapons unserviceable for lack of parts (MND).

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: trained for counter-insurgency, not conventional war (Korean War article); most battalions had not completed battalion-level training.

count.note: 91 M3 105 mm howitzers (ROK MND); plus 960 81 mm and 60 mm mortars, excluded. KPA advantage in howitzers ~6:1.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: short-barrel M3 105 mm with ~6.5 km range, outranged by KPA 122 mm.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: US KMAG-trained, small and new artillery arm.

count.note: Educated guess: M8 Greyhound armoured cars of the ROK cavalry regiment (Appleman ch. 2 gives 27, from memory; not fetched). The ROK had no tanks.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25. Evidence: 37 mm armoured cars useless against T-34s.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: as the army.

count.note: ROK Navy at the outbreak: 6,956 men and 33 vessels of various types (ROK Navy figures and US NHC, ROK Navy article): one PC-701 subchaser Baekdusan, ex-US YMS minesweepers and ex-Japanese craft.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25. Evidence: small second-hand craft.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: NHC called the ROKN the most aggressive and effective ROK service in 1950; sank a KPA troop transport off Pusan on 25-26 June.

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: no corps headquarters, piecemeal commitment, premature Han bridge demolition trapped ROK units north of the river (Korean War article).

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.25-0.5. Evidence: 1948 Yosu-Sunchon mutiny and purges; 95,000 fell to under 22,000 in five days; but the 6th Division held at Chunchon.

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.25-0.5. Evidence: surprise attack on a Sunday with troops on leave; mass retreat and defections in the first week.

weapons.note: Anchor: between 7 (1905) and 8 (1943). Evidence: M1 rifles and 105 mm M3 howitzers but no tanks, no effective AT weapons, no heavy artillery.

armor.note: Anchor: 7 (armoured cars). Evidence: only M8 armoured cars; no tanks.

ships.note: Anchor: 7. Evidence: a 600-ton subchaser and minesweepers.

fortification.note: Anchor: 7 (trenches). Evidence: field positions on the parallel only.

logistics.note: Anchor: 7 (railways) to 8 (motor transport). Evidence: railways, but division vehicle holdings 52% of TO&E with <40% serviceable (MND).

communications.note: Anchor: 7-8. Evidence: US radios at regiment/division, KMAG advisers; poor inter-division coordination.

isr.note: Anchor: ISR 7 (aerial reconnaissance). Evidence: L-4/L-5 liaison planes only; ignored warnings of the build-up.

air.note: Anchor: air 7 (1914 aircraft level of capability). Evidence: 20-22 trainers and liaison aircraft, no combat aircraft (ROKAF article, MND).

cyber.note: No computer networks in 1950; cyber did not exist as a military domain.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: COW milex ROK 1950 = 32,000 thousand current US$ (~US$32M) against a GNP of very roughly US$1-1.5bn current: ~2-3% (low); mid allows US-funded equipment; high = wartime 1950.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: The South was the agricultural half of colonial Korea; light industry (textiles) around Seoul, Pusan and Taegu; power came from the North until 1948.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - agricultural share of the labour force (share of food output not eaten by the farm population; no calorie self-sufficiency adjustment). World Bank WDI Database Archives (version 1999 Apr), SL.AGR.TOTL.ZS "Labor force in agriculture (% of total)" (ILO-based) South Korea 1960 = 61.3% (the series starts in 1960, so it is the floor for 1950). 1950 share extrapolated to ~72% (61-80%) on the 1960-70 trend of ~1.2 points a year. Grade C. Share 72.0% (range 61.3-80.0%) -> 0.28 (0.2-0.387).

annualCohort.note: Educated guess: Males reaching 18 per year: ~20M population, ~2% per single-year cohort, halved.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: Mostly unpaved roads south of the 38th parallel.

railKm.note: Educated guess: Southern share of colonial Korea's railway (Kyongbu Seoul-Pusan, Honam, Chungang, Kyongui south of the parallel).

majorPorts.note: Educated guess: Pusan, Inchon, Mokpo, Kunsan, Yosu, Masan, Pohang; Pusan was the UN lifeline.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess: Korea Shipping Corporation fleet of ex-Japanese and US-leased ships; deadweight guess.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess: ROK divisions lacked vehicles (52% of TO&E) and depended on rail; fought close to their bases.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: Cattle (ox-carts) of the southern farm economy; A-frame porters carried much front-line supply.

nuclearWarheads.note: FAS via OWID: no Korean nuclear weapons in 1950.

chokepoints: Uijongbu and Kaesong-Munsan corridors to Seoul

homeDefense.note: 1.1 row: familiar terrain and local supply; population support divided by the 1948-50 insurgency; no fortified line.

notes: Snapshot date 25 June 1950 (KPA invasion). Territory and population: the ROK south of the 38th parallel (border ref hb:1945:Korea (USA), the nearest basemap at or before 1950). activePersonnel = ROK armed forces 105,752 per the ROK MND Institute for Military History (fetched via web.archive.org, 1K29.pdf, compiling the 2004 official history); US Military Advisory Group (KMAG, ~500 men) and the National Police are excluded. The ROK had no tanks and no combat aircraft (20-22 trainers and liaison aircraft only), so those roles are omitted; aircraft counts are in the notes only. All equipment was US-supplied; no domestic arms production, production empty. Appleman (CMH) could not be fetched (HTTP 403; archive.org copy lending-only), so the M8 count is an educated guess. Weakest numbers: infantry share of the army, trained reserves and logistics infrastructure (educated guesses).
